images.caption: Beach at Ferryside. View towards Ferry Point. As the name suggests, this was an historically important crossing place on the Towy estuary. It was on the medieval pilgrims' route to St. David's cathedral. After the railway opened in 1852, holidaymakers used to arrive by train at Ferryside and cross by boat to Llansteffan. Ferries no longer operate from here.

description: This walk follows a section of the Wales Coast Path from Ferryside to Kidwelly in Carmarthenshire. The route runs for just under 5 miles following country trails south east from Ferryside to Kidwelly via the village of Llansaint. There's some fine countryside and coastal views with the Towy River Estuary to the west. On the way you could stop off at Llansaint for some refreshments.
